subject: Boundary handoff: temporary processing window request & DPA addendum path
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liao <emma.liao@orbitalhealth.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Boundary handoff: temporary processing window request & DPA addendum path

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Orbital's security team raised a last-minute question about short-lived cross-region processing when we need transient failover for availability (e.g., a regional outage). To keep things concrete, they're asking for:

- a clearly scoped temporary processing window (max duration we can activate transient cross-hop),
- confirmation of which subprocessors might be involved during that window, and
- a short contractual rubric we can add to the DPA that limits purpose, duration, and auditability.

Attached is a draft DPA addendum (DPA_addendum_v3.pdf) and a short ops runbook (ops_runbook_transient-egress.xlsx) that shows how we limit data movement to cache-only prefixes, KMS key usage, and automatic rollback triggers. High-level proposal from our side:

1) Temporary window: up to 72 hours per incident, single activation per 30-day rolling period unless mutually escalated.
2) Purpose-limited: only to maintain availability for live inference requests; no batch exports or analytics in that window.
3) Subprocessor roster: AWS (us-west-2), GCP (us-west1) as failover pools — we will not engage any additional subprocessors without notice.
4) Auditability: full trace-level logs retained for 90 days tied to the incident (we can extend if you need).

If that aligns with Orbital's risk appetite we can push the DPA addendum into DocuSign and schedule a short run-through with your security ops to show the rollback and telemetry.

Proposed next steps:
- Emma: confirm whether 72h / single activation is acceptable or suggest a different guardrail.
- Marissa: if okay, please prepare the DocuSign packet and tag legal for the small redline on Section 3 (purpose/duration).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick screen share to walk the ops runbook.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Emma Liao <emma.liao@orbitalhealth.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orbitalhealth.io
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 10:21:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Boundary handoff: temporary processing window request & DPA addendum path

Ben —

Appreciate the clear proposal and the attachments. A few clarifying questions from Orbital's side before we can greenlight language into our DPA:

1) What exactly moves during the 72h window? Your note says "cache-only prefixes" — we need a short enumeration of data classes (PII, hashed ids, derived vectors) that will be allowed to cross-region.
2) KMS: will the same customer-managed key (CMK) be used across the failover region, or will Redwood use a separate envelope key for the transient pool? We need assurance that keys are never exported.
3) Subprocessor detail: you list AWS/GCP locations; please confirm the actual process to bring the instances up (is it automated routing or manual runbook initiation?) and whether any third-party monitoring vendors (PagerDuty, Datadog) will get telemetry during the incident.
4) Audit log retention: 90 days is short for our compliance team — can you retain raw audit events for 12 months and provide summarized incident reports within 5 business days?

Also include a copy of the redline you propose for our DPA (so our legal can do a quick review). If we can get concrete answers to the above, Procurement can prepare the DocuSign routing on our side.

Thanks —
Emma
Emma Liao
DPO, Orbital Health

Subject: Re: Boundary handoff: temporary processing window request & DPA addendum path

Emma — thanks for the quick follow-up and good questions. Below are concrete answers and an updated redline summary included in the attached DPA_addendum_v3.pdf. Short answers first, details after.

Short answers:
- Allowed data classes during transient hop: ephemeral request payloads and derived embeddings only; no raw PII, no long-term storage, no analytics exports.
- KMS: we will use customer-managed envelope keys where customers provide them; for Orbital (per our standard onboarding) you can provide a CMK in your AWS account which we use via key policies — keys are never exported.
- Bring-up process: fully automated routing policy with manual ops gating for activation (two-person approval in the Canary control plane). Datadog will receive telemetry (metrics/traces) but we can redact sensitive payload fields; PagerDuty is used for paging only, not for log storage.
- Audit retention: we can retain raw incident logs for 12 months (secure S3 with restricted access) and will produce a 5-business-day incident summary with scope and token counts.

Detailed notes:
1) Data classes: to be explicit — the only artefacts that may cross-region are tokenized request content (transient, not persisted beyond cache TTL), and derived vector/embedding outputs used to satisfy the live request. User identifiers will be hashed and truncated; no unencrypted PII will be written to durable storage.

2) KMS & key handling: please see Section 2.2 of the attached addendum. For Orbital we propose the standard CMK-on-customer-account model. Envelope keys are used per-region; envelope wrapping is performed in the region where the CMK is hosted; Redwood does not export the CMK.

3) Subprocessor and ops flow: activation is an automated routing switch but requires manual approval. We will only instantiate capacity from the named cloud providers listed in the addendum; we will not spin up 3rd-party vendors for storage or analytics. Datadog collects anonymized telemetry; logs with request payloads are stored in a locked bucket with limited access.

4) Auditability: raw logs retained 12 months; we will give an incident summary and a CSV with request timestamps/token counts within 5 business days.

Next steps:
- Emma: if the answers above are acceptable, we'll send the DocuSign packet and propose a 30-minute runbook demo (ops walkthrough) for your security ops.
- Marissa: please prepare DocuSign using the provided link and include the redline in the envelope.

Attachment: DPA_addendum_v3.pdf (redline + final text) and ops_runbook_transient-egress.xlsx (ops checklist).

Cheers,
Ben

Emma / Ben —

Thanks for the back-and-forth. Legal has reviewed the proposed 72-hour single-activation window and the purpose limitation language in the attached redline. We want to be explicit in the DPA addendum: any activation must include (a) written notice to Orbital within 2 business hours, (b) a post-incident summary within 5 business days, and (c) a maximum of 72 hours per activation, with extensions allowed only by mutual written agreement.

We will also add a short clause that requires Redwood to provide proof of subprocessor roster for the activation period (stack trace + instance IDs) and that any monitoring/telemetry vendors will be contractually prohibited from storing request payloads.

Marissa — please coordinate DocuSign routing and include the HubSpot deal (OHL-2026-042) in the envelope so Procurement can mark execution. Emma — once your team confirms the 12-month log retention requirement is acceptable we will finalize and route.

-Markus
